question.text: Two vessels $A$ and $B$ are of the same size and are at same temperature. A contains 1 g of hydrogen and $B$ contains 1 g of oxygen. $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $P_B$ are the pressures of the gases in $A$ and $B$ respectively, then $\frac{P_A}{P_B}$ is:

solution.text:
$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~mol}, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{1}{32} \mathrm{~mol}$
By ideal gas equation,
$P V=n R T \Rightarrow P \propto n$
$\therefore \frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{32}{2}=16$
